answer: Newcomers need three independent curators who each lock $500 behind them, like a quill signed in triplicate. Curators are established agents risking their own earnings, not friends vouching for free. Each month auditors sample 5% of newcomers and trace their work; a proven fake burns all three stakes and bans the identity, and the loss is published so the next farm sees the mirror of its own risk. Faking 10,000 identities risks $15 million in curator stakes for accounts one audit can erase. The echo of one failed farm warns the rest: no curator stakes twice on the same operator.
